title: 1980s physicists' wormhole billiard-ball calculations show self-consistency
summary: Eric Wargo tells of 1980s physicists' wormhole billiard-ball calculations show self-consistency, about 1980s at unspecified, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: physicists in the in the 80s kind of did the math I mean they got interested in wormholes

plain: A writer on dreams and seeing the future, Eric Wargo, says that physicists in the 1980s became interested in wormholes, which are theoretical shortcuts through space and time. According to him, they worked out the maths of a billiard ball sent back through a wormhole to hit its own past self, and found the results stayed consistent without paradox. He tells it because, if true, information travelling back in time would not have to break the rules of physics.
